bib.title: WIKIQA: A Challenge Dataset for Open-Domain Question Answering
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 2015 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP), pages 2013-2018

question: Does the QASENT (TREC-QA) answer sentence selection benchmark misrepresent natural open-domain QA, and what does a more natural dataset, including questions with no correct sentence, show?
hypothesis: QASENT's lexical-overlap candidate selection inflates the performance of word matching methods in more natural settings.
contributions: WIKIQA: 3,047 Bing-log questions with 29,258 candidate Wikipedia summary sentences and crowdsourced labels
Comparison of several systems on answer sentence selection on both QASENT and WIKIQA
Proposal of the answer triggering task with question-level precision, recall and F1, plus a feature study

method.summary: Questions were sampled from Bing query logs and linked by clicks to Wikipedia pages; all sentences of the page summary are candidates, labelled by crowd workers. Seven baselines (word counts, LCLR, Paragraph Vector, CNN and two combinations) are compared on QASENT and WIKIQA by MAP/MRR, and the best (CNN-Cnt) is evaluated on answer triggering.
method.task: answer sentence selection and answer triggering (open-domain QA)

datasets.name: WIKIQA
datasets.size: 3,047 questions; 29,258 sentences; 1,473 answer sentences; 1,805 questions without an answer
datasets.split: random split 70% train (2,118 q, 20,360 sent), 10% dev (296 q, 2,733 sent), 20% test (633 q, 6,165 sent)
datasets.source: Bing query logs May 1 2010 to July 31 2011; Wikipedia summary sections; released at http://aka.ms/WikiQA
datasets.preprocessing: Question-like queries picked by heuristics (WH-word start or question mark; entity queries filtered), about 2% of queries kept; only queries from at least 5 unique users with clicks to Wikipedia; 3,050 sampled by frequency. Labelled by three crowd workers per question in a two-stage UI, disputed sentences re-verified, majority vote. Answer phrases added by authors, at most two per sentence, not used in experiments. For MAP/MRR, questions without answers are removed.

datasets.name: QASENT
datasets.size: 227 questions; 8,478 sentences; 928 answers (train 94 q, dev 65, test 68)
datasets.split: settings of Yih et al. (2013); only 94 train questions have human annotations
datasets.source: TREC 8-13 QA tracks, Wang et al. (2007)
datasets.preprocessing: sentences kept only if they share one or more non-stopwords with the question; questions without correct answers discarded

datasets.name: UIUC Question Classification
datasets.preprocessing: used to train a logistic regression question classifier for the QClass feature

models.name: Word Cnt
models.architecture: count of question non-stopwords in the answer sentence

models.name: Wgt Word Cnt
models.architecture: word count re-weighted by IDF of question words

models.name: LCLR
models.architecture: Yih et al. (2013) lexical semantic model: word/lemma matching, WordNet, vector-space lexical semantics; no NE matching features; reimplemented

models.name: PV
models.architecture: Paragraph Vector, Distributed Bag of Words version; score = cosine of question and sentence vectors

models.name: CNN
models.architecture: bigram CNN with average pooling (Yu et al. 2014)
models.init_from: pre-trained word2vec embeddings (Mikolov et al. 2013) as input

models.name: PV-Cnt / CNN-Cnt
models.architecture: logistic regression combining PV or CNN score with the two word-count features

training.objective: logistic regression classifier for the combined models; the other models' objectives are not stated
training.seq_len: inferred: sentences truncated to 40 tokens for CNN

other.threshold: answer-triggering score threshold tuned for F1 on the dev set because of skewed class distribution

inference.samples: not stated; single run per system apparently
inference.retrieval: candidates are all sentences of the clicked Wikipedia page summary

metrics.name: MAP
metrics.definition: mean average precision of ranking correct sentences among a question's candidates (questions with answers only)

metrics.name: MRR
metrics.definition: mean reciprocal rank of the first correct sentence

metrics.name: Question-level precision/recall/F1 (answer triggering)
metrics.definition: A question is positive if its pool has one or more correct sentences; only the top-scored sentence is considered; correct if its score exceeds a threshold and it is a labelled answer

eval.protocol: Fixed train/dev/test split; no seeds or significance tests reported.

limits: Candidates come only from the Wikipedia summary paragraph, so recall of the candidate pool is not tested.
Answer-triggering study covers only one system (CNN-Cnt) with a few features; authors say F1 leaves large room.
No seeds, variance or significance tests; CNN reimplementation performs slightly worse than Yu et al. (2014).
Model details (optimizer, learning rate, CNN size) are not given.
Dated: neural sentence-ranking baselines of 2014; later models far surpass them.
